status: Visual proposal only. Not a sliced, seam-validated tileset; not applied to Unity or deployed.

references.basis: Official Exploration video, visually inspected. Long surface bands, dark lower material and irregular hanging accents reduce the prominence of repeated structures. Internal asset/shader workflow is not established by this observation.

proposal.grid: Preserve existing 128px grid; let visual features cross multiple cells.
layers: Long compatible surface strips with shallow irregularity
Continuous low-contrast fill and broad multi-cell strata
Continuous depth shading rather than shading reset per cell

prompts.generation:
Create one high-quality wide 16:9 game environment material concept image for an original dark fantasy 2D metroidvania called Unfinished Sketchbook. This is a visual proposal for the STARTING FLOOR in region 1, "Crumpled Paper Cavern / Blank Beginning Path", not a finished tile atlas.
Art direction: atmospheric refined high-resolution 2D game illustration, the quiet somber environmental readability of ENDER LILIES, combined with our own graphite-and-paper underground world. Restrained stylized material realism, about 70 percent detail, broad softly rounded forms, no pixel art, no scribbly hand-drawing, no photorealistic gritty micro-noise.
Composition: strict side elevation, orthographic, no perspective top face, no vanishing points. Show an uninterrupted long horizontal WALKABLE GROUND cross-section across the entire width, visually equivalent to about 12-15 game cells but with absolutely NO visible tile grid or cell-sized repeated motifs. The ground surface is at approximately 53 percent of image height, leaving enough empty dark cave air above to judge silhouette. Mostly level playable surface with small shallow irregular bumps. Near the right quarter one gentle round-edged raised shelf, about one cell higher, joins the same solid landmass; softly rounded inside and outside corners. The ground fills the image below, rather than floating. Backdrop is very quiet dark slate-gray enclosed cavern, just a few extremely faint large folded-paper silhouettes; NO landscape, horizon, ornate scenery, buildings, characters, enemies, UI, letters, labels, grids, numbers, arrows or logos.
Foreground material: compressed charcoal-gray soil mingled with soft worn paper strata, subtle graphite sheen only on occasional broad planes. The paper is old and mineral-like, not a pile of loose white pages. Desaturated warm-gray paper edges are sparse, never bright white. Elegant long shallow folds drift diagonally and horizontally across multiple imagined cells, changing width and gently merging into quieter areas. Make asymmetrical patches of different sizes: some almost featureless wide dark surfaces, some medium soft overlapping layers, a few small dull fragments. The viewer must NOT be able to count how many tiles were used. No central boulder per cell; no row of evenly sized stones; no regular scallops; no repeating oval stamps; no dense cobblestone pattern; no equal spacing; no tessellated rock cracks. Texture continuity must cross arbitrary cell boundaries instead of restarting.
Surface edge: a thin legible ash-gray ragged contact edge, intermittent subdued highlight, small irregular compressed-paper lips and rounded soil lumps; no smooth neon outline and no deep grass carpet. Keep the imagined physical walking line clearly readable. Sparse tiny blunt graphite rootlets can hang in two or three irregular groups to break up visual rhythm, but do not dominate or obscure the ground.
Depth: near-surface material is readable, then progressively fades downward into near-black charcoal over the full visible ground thickness. The lowest third is almost completely dark, with no repeated bright motifs. Shadow field is continuous across the whole mass, never a separate gradient or black border for each tile. Wall/step material bends and blends with the floor with rounded transitions.
Lighting: neutral soft cool-gray ambient light, subdued values; no dramatic spotlight baked into the material, no bloom, no blue magic, no saturated colors. Separate the distant cavern wall through lower contrast. Make the floor the central subject. This should feel like a coherent length of naturally eroded graphite-paper earth that can later be divided into 128px modules, not like a row of standalone texture squares. Output only the single polished concept image, edge-to-edge, no presentation frame.
prompts.refinement: Edit this terrain concept image. Preserve its exact composition, long uninterrupted floor, raised shelf on the right, natural non-repeating cross-cell strata, subdued graphite-gray palette, quiet enclosed cavern, and progressive fade into near-black deep earth. Change only rendering/material detail: make it clearly a polished 2D dark-fantasy GAME ILLUSTRATION rather than photographic rock. Reduce fine noise, granular grit and tiny fissures by about half; consolidate tiny details into broad soft-edged matte value planes. Soften pointed sharp paper fragments into worn rounded layered edges, avoiding polygonal shard silhouettes. Keep sparse long subtle folded-paper strata irregularly crossing wide sections, interspersed with large calm areas; do not replace them with a row of boulders or repeating stamped motifs. Keep crisp readable but shallow uneven walkable edge, no thick highlight stripe and no perspective top plane. Preserve depth and moody quality similar to environmental painting in ENDER LILIES, but retain this original graphite-and-compressed-paper material. No outlines around every material patch. No new elements, no labels, no grid, no text, no character. Overall detail target 70/100, stylized realism 75/100, not cartoonish or cute.
